guide.summary: Use a Notion public connection (OAuth 2.0) with only the Read content capability. Each customer authorizes the app and selects the pages to share through the OAuth page picker. Choose the installation scope at creation, since it cannot be changed later. Test with one representative workspace and a page you select during authorization. Do not request Insert content or Update content. Whether the app needs provider review or a Marketplace listing for customer rollout is not established by the supplied sources.

findings.title: Public connection OAuth fits customer workspaces
findings.detail: Notion documents public connections as OAuth connections that each authorizing user installs into their own workspace, with a per-user access token.

evidence.quote: A public connection is an OAuth connection that users install into their Notion workspaces. Unlike internal connections , which are scoped to a single workspace with a static token, public
connections follow the OAuth 2.0 protocol: each user who authorizes the connection receives their own access token, scoped to their workspace.

findings.title: Read content capability covers both read actions
findings.detail: Read content gives access to read existing content, including retrieving pages. Missing capabilities return 403.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to both requested read actions

​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Customers choose pages during authorization
findings.detail: Public connections use the OAuth page picker, where users choose which pages to grant access to during the authorization flow.

evidence.quote: Page access: Internal connections require workspace members to manually share pages via the “Add connections” menu. Public connections use the OAuth page picker, where users choose which pages to grant

steps.title: Test read of shared page titles
steps.detail: Call GET /v1/pages/{page_id} with the OAuth access token and Notion-Version 2026-03-11. Expected response: a page object whose properties include the title. Boundary check: request a page you did not select during authorization, expecting 404 for missing access. This is a read-only GET; do not run write calls.
steps.doneWhen: Selected page returns its title property, and the unselected page returns 404 with no writes made.

steps.title: Read markdown of a customer-shared Notion page
steps.detail: Use the OAuth access token from the customer authorization flow. Send a GET request to /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown with markdown_version=v2 and the Notion-Version header. Representative input: the page ID of a page the customer selected in the page picker. Expected successful result: the response contains the page's markdown content. Notion-flavored v2 markdown is recommended, and v1 is deprecated. Content may be truncated for very large pages, and child pages not shared with the connection are not included. Boundary check: send the same GET to the ID of a page the customer did not share. Expect 404 (missing access) or 403 (missing capability). Confirm that the response contains no page content and that no create or update request was made.
steps.doneWhen: The selected page returns markdown content with a 200 response. The unshared page returns 404 or 403 with no content, and the test used only GET requests with no write effect.

evidence.quote: Set the markdown_version query parameter to v2 to get Notion-flavored Markdown instead. v2 is recommended. v1 is deprecated. It’s the default on current Notion-Versions. See Markdown versions .
